text:
alex: Heads-up: p99 latency spike on us-west-2 serving cluster, started ~1873012000. Ops alert: KV prefix hit-rate dropped from ~92% to 6% on pool-8.

ops-bot: [ALERT] 1873012057 - us-west-2 pool-8: p99 420ms (baseline 120ms), kv_prefix_hitrate 6% -> paging on-call.

maria: Looking at flamegraphs now. Kernel-selection fell back from AVX2-specialized path to generic fallback for several shards. See sample: 
```
shard=pool-8-12 kernel=generic seq=512 tokens=256 cpu=84% mem=6.1G
shard=pool-8-12 kernel=avx2 seq=64 tokens=64 cpu=36% mem=2.2G
```

priya: Hmm that's odd — why did kernel fallback trigger? Last deploy had batching-heuristic tweak to favor larger micro-batches for high-concurrency tenants. Could be changing seq distribution and pushing kernel choice heuristics.

sam: I pulled request logs: batching policy flag `enable_aggressive_grouping=true` rolled to us-west-2 yesterday 03:12. Rollout note said "improves throughput for long-seqs".

alex: The KV prefix hitrate collapse timeline matches the rollout window. Could larger batches be expanding prefix cardinality (different prefixes in same batch) and causing prefix-key cache churn?

maria: Profiler snapshot: when kernel=generic we see 2.7x more KV lookups per request (more prefix probes), and GC pressure spikes. That explains both hit-rate drop and latency increase.

priya: Also noticed tenant T-472 has very high prefix cardinality in their requests (lots of per-request metadata in the prompt). Noisy neighbor candidate.

sam: Running quick query against prefix stats: 
```
SELECT prefix, count(*) FROM kv_access WHERE pool='pool-8' AND ts > 1873011800 GROUP BY prefix ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 20;
-- top prefixes are low-frequency, tail explosion.
```

maria: Mitigation idea 1: flip `enable_aggressive_grouping=false` for pool-8 to restore previous batching shape -> should push kernel selection back to avx2 path. Mitigation idea 2: temporary tenant throttle for T-472 or route T-472 to dedicated shard.

alex: Quick actions then: Priya, can you stomp the batching flag for pool-8? Sam can you open a tenant throttle ticket and add T-472 to it? Maria will prepare rollback and a kernel-selection telemetry patch.

priya: On it. Pushing config change now to pool-8: `enable_aggressive_grouping=false`. Will watch.

ops-bot: [DEPLOY] 1873012389 - config change applied to pool-8 by priya.

maria: After ~60s of the flag flip we already see kernel-selection back to avx2 for many shards and prefix hit-rate climbing: 6% -> 58%. CPU usage down and p99 trending to baseline.

sam: Opened ticket INF-7654 to throttle T-472 and to add a routing rule. Assigned to infra-oncall.

alex: Good. Longer-term: we need 1) stricter guardrails on batching heuristics when tail-cardinality tenants present, 2) kernel-selection should use a softer fallback with a brief probe window to avoid mass fallbacks, and 3) per-tenant prefix-cardinality monitoring + auto-throttle. I'll draft RFC.

priya: Agreed. I'll also add a canary to future batching rollouts that measures prefix-cardinality delta and aborts if >x%.

maria: Follow-up for eng-runtime: collect kernel-choice + kv_probe_rate histograms per shard at 10s granularity and create a Grafana panel so we can catch this before p99 jumps.

alex: Nice. For incident record: root cause = batching-heuristic rollout caused larger micro-batches that increased per-request prefix-cardinality and triggered kernel fallback to generic path -> increased KV probes, cache churn, and p99 spike. Mitigations = revert batching flag, throttle noisy tenant, telemetry & canary changes.

sam: Marking incident as "mitigated" for now. Will continue collecting post-mortem data. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll attach profiler dumps and the flamegraph diff to INF-7654.

alex: Thanks team. Follow-up doc pls in eng-runtime/insights.
